title: Where does the lift reach from floor plus two?
description: The lift starts on floor plus two and the minus three button is pressed. The movement is added to the starting floor, the floors are counted down one at a time, and the answer is checked by going back up. The expression for the movement is written with the answer.
teaching_notes: One idea: adding a negative movement takes the lift to a lower floor. Watch for students who add the numbers three and two and say the lift goes up.

video_script.why: The child writes starting floor plus movement as an expression, and sees that adding a negative movement ends on a lower floor.
video_script.substitution: the book's own lift starting on floor plus two and moving three floors down
video_script.anchor: the lift of {{NAME_10}}, starting on floor +2 and pressing −3
video_script.payoff_line: Adding a negative movement takes the lift down.

final_answer.spoken: floor minus one, the Toy Store, because plus two and minus three make minus one

names.{{NAME_10}}: the multi-storey block of floors above and below the ground, used as the model for integers

never_show: the target floor before the answer
maths_rules: Start +2, movement −3 means three floors down: +1, then 0, then −1.
(+2) + (−3) = −1, and floor −1 is the Toy Store.
Check: three floors up from −1 gives 0, +1, +2, back to the start.
video_script.design: One idea: a negative movement takes the lift down. One lift picture throughout; the floors are counted along the side. Method as in the solved example.
